title: Supported products and Cartier interchange on ordinary etale sites
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme on which a prime $\ell$ is invertible, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Work on small etale sites with roots-of-unity twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Write $H_C^a(X,\Lambda(b))$ for the cohomology of the derived functor of sections vanishing off a closed subset $C$ [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. There are natural associative bilinear products
$$H_C^a(X,\Lambda(b))\otimes H_D^{a'}(X,\Lambda(b'))\to H_{C\cap D}^{a+a'}(X,\Lambda(b+b'))$$
with sign $(-1)^{aa'}$ on interchange. For nested closed supports $Z\subset Y\subset X$ there are associative action products $H_Z^a(Y,\Lambda(b))\otimes H_Y^{a'}(X,\Lambda(b'))\to H_Z^{a+a'}(X,\Lambda(b+b'))$, satisfying the projection formula for classes on $Y$. Under the supported-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] these action products are composition of supported morphisms; after adjunction they are exceptional composition. These products commute with pullback of pairs, open restriction, and coefficient reduction.
For a line bundle $L$ with a trivialization $s$ off $C$, let $e_C(L,s)$ be the supported Kummer first Chern class [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology, lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. For two such pairs, with their supports enlarged to a common closed set when necessary,
$$e(L\otimes M,s\otimes t)=e(L,s)+e(M,t),\qquad e(L^\vee,s^\vee)=-e(L,s).$$
For an effective Cartier divisor $D$, $e_D(\mathcal O_X(D),1)$ is the class of $c_{D,\Lambda}$ in [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], whereas $e_D(\mathcal I_D,1)$ is its negative [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. A pseudo-divisor class defines an operator $G_{L,s}:H^a(C,\Lambda(b))\to H_C^{a+2}(X,\Lambda(b+1))$ by this action. For every closed $W\subset C$, the same nested action extends it to $G_{L,s}:H_W^a(C,\Lambda(b))\to H_W^{a+2}(X,\Lambda(b+1))$; this extension is used in iterated operators below, so both Cartier composites have domain $H^a(D_1\cap D_2,\Lambda(b))$ and codomain $H_{D_1\cap D_2}^{a+4}(X,\Lambda(b+2))$. Its restriction to $C$ is multiplication by $c_1(L|_C)$. For a class $x\in H^a(X,\Lambda(b))$, the image of $G_{L,s}(x|_C)$ in $H^{a+2}(X,\Lambda(b+1))$ after forgetting the support is $x\cdot c_1(L)$. If two effective Cartier divisors $D_1,D_2$ meet transversely, meaning each restricts to an effective Cartier divisor on the other, their ideal-normalized operators obey
$$G_{D_1\subset X}\,G_{D_1\cap D_2\subset D_1}=G_{D_2\subset X}\,G_{D_1\cap D_2\subset D_2}.$$
The equality uses the canonical identification of the intersections and twists; both operators use $e(\mathcal I_D,1)$. No regularity of $X$ is required.

source.place: Expose XVI, section 2.1 (pseudo-divisors), Lemma 2.2.2.4; supported pairings in Proposition 2.2.3.2 and proof of Theorem 2.3.2, pp. 235-236 (associativity and transverse Cartier interchange).

proof.text:
Put $P_C=(i_C)_*\Lambda_C$ and let $\rho_C:\Lambda_X\to P_C$ be constant restriction. The open-closed short exact sequence, applied to $\Lambda_X$, identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_X(P_C,M)$ with $\ker(\Gamma(X,M)\to\Gamma(X\setminus C,M))$: precompose with $\rho_C$ and evaluate at $1$. Derive this identity on bounded-below injective resolutions. The supported-Hom theorem and the support-restriction triangle (take its first support to be all of $X$) give
$$H_C^a(X,\Lambda(b))=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)}(P_C,\Lambda_X(b)[a]).$$
These are the same identifications, since both are induced by the preceding underived kernel identity. In particular forgetting support is precomposition with $\rho_C$, and restriction to a closed subscheme is ordinary inverse image of the represented morphism with the closed-constant exchange. All coefficient complexes here are bounded below, including every shifted line sheaf used below.

For $\alpha:P_C\to\Lambda(b)[a]$ and $\beta:P_D\to\Lambda(b')[a']$, define their product by
$$P_{C\cap D}\xrightarrow{\mu_{C,D}^{-1}}P_C\otimes^L P_D\xrightarrow{\alpha\otimes\beta}\Lambda(b)[a]\otimes^L\Lambda(b')[a']\xrightarrow{t_{a,a'}}\Lambda(b+b')[a+a'].$$
The closed-constant tensor lemma supplies the specified associative, symmetric multiplication $\mu$, and the twist lemma supplies locally free rank-one coefficient lines. The multiplication of signed powers is associative and symmetric: on any local basis it sends $e^b\otimes e^{b'}$ to $e^{b+b'}$, including negative powers by evaluation. Apply the source-system cup-calculus lemma with labels the closed supports and meet their intersection. Its hypotheses are exactly these flatness and coherence statements. It gives bilinearity, associativity and interchange sign $(-1)^{aa'}$ for every integer degree and twist. Bilinearity factors the pairing through the tensor product of the cohomology groups. No purity or regularity assertion is used.

source.place: Tags 0FPL and 0FPM (associative and commutative cup products), applied via the signed tensor-morphism/source-system refinements

proof.text:
For $k:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ and $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$, represent $u\in H_Z^a(Y,\Lambda(b))$ by $k_*\Lambda_Z\to\Lambda_Y(b)[a]$, and $v\in H_Y^{a'}(X,\Lambda(b'))$ by $P_Y\to\Lambda_X(b')[a']$. Closed pushforward is exact: closed immersions are finite and finite direct image is exact. Identify $i_*k_*\Lambda_Z=P_Z$ by composition of direct images. Let
$$p_{i,N,K}:i_*N\otimes^L K\longrightarrow i_*(N\otimes^Li^*K)$$
be the canonical projection map, adjoint to the inverse-image tensor comparison followed by the ordinary adjunction counit. For a shifted twist line $K$ it is an isomorphism: locally trivialize the line and use the projection map's unit and shift laws. Its inverse identifies $i_*\Lambda_Y(b)[a]$ with $P_Y(b)[a]$. Define
$$u\cdot v=(-1)^{a a'}v(b)[a]\circ p_{i,\Lambda_Y,\Lambda_X(b)[a]}^{-1}\circ i_*u.$$
The displayed sign is the Koszul comparison for composing homogeneous morphisms with the fixed $t_{a,a'}$: moving the second degree past the first shift contributes $(-1)^{a a'}$. This is the shifted tensor action, expressed as composition of supported morphisms; for every Cartier factor its degree is two and this sign is $1$. This gives the nested action with support $Z$; the same formula applies to every further closed support in $Y$. Its associativity is composition associativity: for degrees $a,a',a''$ both signs are $(-1)^{a a'+a a''+a' a''}$, and both parenthesizations are the successive pushed morphisms, with all line factors reassociated by $(n\otimes l)\otimes l'\mapsto n\otimes(ll')$. The signed shift comparisons agree by the shifted tensor-calculus lemma.

source.place: XVI §2.1, pp. 228–229, composition description of Gys; Proposition 2.2.3.2, p. 233, canonical action pairing. Projection map: Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0B56

proof.text: Projection for a class on $Y$ is the same composition formula with its first support all of $Y$. Thus $(u\cup y)\cdot v=u\cdot(y\cdot v)$, with the indicated shifts, by the associativity just checked. For an ambient class $x$, naturality of $p_{i,N,K}$ in $K$ says that tensoring by $x$ before the projection map equals $i_*i^*x$ after it. This gives $(i^*x)\cdot v=x\cup v$, including any smaller support in $Y$. This is the projection formula used here. Finally the right adjoints $Ri^!$ and $Rk^!$ exist for closed immersions. With the homogeneous-composition sign fixed in Step 3, a composite $i_*k_*\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{i_*u}i_*\Lambda_Y(b)[a]\xrightarrow{v(b)[a]}\Lambda_X(b+b')[a+a']$ transposes by applying first the $i_*\dashv Ri^!$ Hom bijection and then the $k_*\dashv Rk^!$ bijection. Their composite is exactly the Hom bijection for $(ik)_*\dashv Rk^!Ri^!$. Including that same shift comparison, this is exceptional composition after adjunction. The line comparison in this displayed composite is the one fixed in Step 3.

source.place: XVI §2.1, p. 229, morphism and composition interpretation; §2.2.3, canonical pairings. Adjunction composition: Stacks categories.tex Tag 0DV0

proof.text: Let $v:X'\to X$, and pull back every closed support scheme-theoretically. Inverse image on constant-coefficient etale modules is exact. The particular closed-constant exchanges $b_{v,C}:v^{-1}P_C\cong P_{C'}$ preserve $\rho$ and $\mu$, and the roots-of-unity comparisons preserve line multiplication and evaluation. Consequently the exact-pullback clause of the source-system cup-calculus lemma applies to Step 2. For Step 3 use finite exchange for each closed immersion, on both the source and target of the pushed morphism. The projection map is the mate of the tensor comparison and counit; replacing these by their inverse-image comparisons gives the same mate, so the defining nested composite pulls back to the composite defining the pulled-back action. More explicitly, before taking mates both maps are the tensor of the pulled-back morphism with the identity followed by the pulled-back counit; the adjunction bijection identifies them. Exchanges compose as constant restriction and inverse image do, so these products preserve identities and compositions of pair maps. Open restriction is the case that $v$ is open. No Cartier hypothesis is needed for this step.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product) and 0B56 (canonical projection mate); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03Q1, finite closed exchange

proof.text: For coefficient reduction $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^N\to B=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, $N\geq n$, use the derived change-of-rings functor $F=-\otimes_A^LB$, not underived tensor on arbitrary complexes. The closed-source scalar comparison gives $F(P_C^A)\cong P_C^B$ without flatness of $B$ over $A$. The map on lines is induced by $z\mapsto z^{\ell^{N-n}}$; etale locally a primitive root is a basis and maps to a primitive-root basis at level $n$, so its scalar extension is an isomorphism. The signed-power lemma extends this comparison to all weights, compatibly with multiplication and evaluation. The ringed-topos tensor-pullback theorem, specialized to the identity topos and $A\to B$, gives $F(K\otimes_A^LL)\cong FK\otimes_B^LFL$. Its compatibility with our products is visible on flat K-flat models: $(p\otimes q)\otimes s\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes(q\otimes s)$ respects multiplication, reassociation and the sign $(-1)^{a'p}$ of the shift comparison. Thus applying $F$ to the defining tensor composite in Step 2 gives exactly the $B$ composite. The closed projection comparison and closed scalar-source maps are induced by these same balanced formulas, so applying $F$ to the composite in Step 3 gives its $B$ counterpart as well. The natural scalar source map is fixed by the coefficient unit, so forgetting support also commutes. This proves reduction compatibility without asserting that reduction is exact on module sheaves.

proof.text: Let $U=X\setminus C$. The frame torsor of $(L,s)$ determines $[L,s]\in H^1(X,U;\mathbf G_m)$ by the relative torsor theorem. Apply the relative connecting map for the exact $\ell^n$-Kummer sequence to define $e_C(L,s)$. The line-torsor correspondence sends tensor product to contracted product. To see addition with the specified sections, form the product of two framed torsors, a $\mathbf G_m\times\mathbf G_m$-torsor, and push it out by multiplication. Relative cohomology of a finite product of coefficient sheaves is the product of relative cohomologies: take the product of the two injective resolutions and their restriction cones. Projection naturality of the relative torsor classification identifies its two coordinates with the given relative classes; multiplication therefore sends them to their sum. The relative Kummer connecting map is a group homomorphism, so $e_C(L\otimes M,s\otimes t)=e_C(L,s)+e_C(M,t)$. The evaluation pairing identifies $(L\otimes L^\vee,s\otimes s^\vee)$ with the trivial framed line; its class is zero. Hence $e_C(L^\vee,s^\vee)=-e_C(L,s)$. When supports differ, restrict both specified sections to the complement of their union and apply the same argument there; forgetting the old support is induced by that restriction of the cones.

source.place: XVI §2.1, pp. 228–229; proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p. 236, addition of framed line classes. Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AJ; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PL

proof.text: The relative torsor theorem makes these classes natural under pullback of the pair, and identifies forgetting the specified section with the ordinary line-torsor class. Naturality of its connecting maps therefore identifies the forgotten $e_C(L,s)$ with the ordinary Kummer $c_1(L)$. Reduction from level $N$ to $n$ uses the commuting Kummer diagram: the map on roots is $z\mapsto z^{\ell^{N-n}}$, the map on the middle $\mathbf G_m$ is the same power, and the map on the right $\mathbf G_m$ is the identity. Indeed $(z^{\ell^{N-n}})^{\ell^n}=z^{\ell^N}$. Its relative connecting square sends $e_C^{(N)}(L,s)$ to $e_C^{(n)}(L,s)$, under Step 6's coefficient identification. For a Cartier $D$, the ordinary supported Kummer theorem identifies $e_D(\mathcal O_X(D),1)$ with $c_{D,\Lambda}$. Since $\mathcal O_X(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ with dual off-divisor trivializations, Step 7 identifies $e_D(\mathcal I_D,1)$ with $-c_{D,\Lambda}$. Pullback retains this Cartier interpretation whenever the inverse-image divisor is Cartier; pullback of the framed line class itself always exists.

source.place: XVI §2.1 and Definition 2.1.1, pp. 228–229 (ideal normalization and its sign); Stacks Tag 03PL, Kummer sequence naturality

proof.text: Define $G_{L,s}(u)=u\cdot e_C(L,s)$ by Step 3 with $Y=C$. For $u\in H_W^a(C,\Lambda(b))$, its represented source after closed pushforward is $P_W$; hence the same formula lands in $H_W^{a+2}(X,\Lambda(b+1))$. This supplies the required extension for every closed $W\subset C$. Pull back the defining morphism to $C$. Closed inverse image cancels its own direct image, and Step 8 identifies the inverse image of $e_C(L,s)$ with $c_1(L|_C)$, because the pulled-back support is all of $C$. Thus restriction of $G$ is multiplication by this class. For $x\in H^a(X,\Lambda(b))$, Step 4 gives $G_{L,s}(x|_C)=x\cup e_C(L,s)$. Precomposition with $\rho_C$ forgets support by Step 1; the restriction/multiplication map defining $\mu$ carries the two constant units to the constant unit on the intersection. Forgetting support therefore gives $x\cup c_1(L)$, as asserted. The pullback and reduction compatibilities of $G$ follow by substituting Step 8 into the defining action and applying Steps 5–6.

source.place: XVI §2.1, p. 229, definition of the operator; Lemma 2.2.2.4, p. 232, restriction of Gys

proof.text:
Write $i:D_1\hookrightarrow X$, $j:D_2\hookrightarrow X$ and $I=D_1\times_XD_2$, with $k:I\hookrightarrow D_1$. Let $e_1,e_2$ be the ideal-normalized supported classes. Transversality ensures that $I$ is Cartier in each $D_i$. Pullback of the local equation and its ideal trivialization identifies $i^*e_2$ with $e(\mathcal I_{I/D_1},1)$ by Step 8 (and likewise with the indices reversed). Apply naturality of the projection map of Step 3 to the morphism $e_2:P_{D_2}\to\Lambda(1)[2]$:
$$p_{i,\Lambda,\Lambda(1)[2]}(1\otimes e_2)=i_*(i^*e_2)\,p_{i,\Lambda,P_{D_2}}.$$
The latter projection map is $\mu_{D_1,D_2}$ under the closed-constant exchange: both are induced by restricting the two constant sections and multiplying them on $I$. Their equality is an equality of degree-zero sheaf maps; the same equality holds on their flat models. Compose the displayed square with $e_1(1)[2]$ and invert the projection isomorphisms. The resulting identity is
$$e_1\star e_2=e_1(1)[2]\circ p_{i,\Lambda,\Lambda(1)[2]}^{-1}\circ i_*(i^*e_2):P_I\to\Lambda(2)[4].$$
Thus the two iterated Cartier class morphisms are respectively $e_1\star e_2$ and $e_2\star e_1$. Step 2 makes them equal, since $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=1$.

source.place: XVI proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p. 236, transverse Cartier operator equality; tensor/projection calculation supplies the interchange argument without a purity theorem

proof.text: For an arbitrary $u\in H^a(I,\Lambda(b))$, push its represented morphism $\Lambda_I\to\Lambda_I(b)[a]$ to $X$, obtaining $\widetilde u:P_I\to P_I(b)[a]$. By Step 3, the two composites of the extended operators in the question are the two class morphisms in Step 10, shifted and twisted by $(b)[a]$, each precomposed with the same $\widetilde u$. Their equality in Step 10 therefore gives equality on every such $u$, in $H_I^{a+4}(X,\Lambda(b+2))$. This also checks the common domain and codomain; no extension of $u$ to $D_1$, $D_2$, or $X$ is assumed. All arguments used only exact closed-support functors, line twists, and the Cartier condition on the two restrictions. In particular no regularity hypothesis on $X$ has entered.
